name: personas
description: Two answer-style personas for Kimi Code: ponytail (lazy senior dev — the smallest complete change, zero over-engineering) and caveman (maximum-terse replies that keep every technical fact), plus review/audit/debt skills and a memory-file compressor.
author: DietrichGebert (ponytail) and Julius Brussee (caveman), ported to Kimi Code by mnshkv
license: Ponytail: MIT; Caveman: Apache-2.0 (pre-3.0 MIT parts under LICENSE-MIT); port © mnshkv

interface.shortDescription: Ponytail lazy-senior-dev mode and caveman terse-answer mode, with review, audit, debt and compression skills
interface.longDescription:
Two personality skills that change how the agent writes code and answers, ported from the ponytail and caveman projects.

Ponytail (MIT, DietrichGebert): "lazy senior developer" mode — solve the whole task with the least new code, no unrequested abstractions or dependencies, mark deliberate shortcuts with `shortcut:` comments. Ships review and audit skills (senior-dev review of a change or a whole repo: bugs, security, load, missing tests, speed, what to cut), a debt ledger that harvests `shortcut:` comments, a measured benchmark scoreboard, and a quick-reference card. Levels: lite, full (default), ultra.

Caveman (Apache-2.0, Julius Brussee): terse-answer persona — answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept verbatim. Levels: caveman, ultracave (maximum compression), megacave (Classical Chinese). caveman-compress shrinks memory files (CLAUDE.md, todo lists) into caveman format to save input tokens, with a readable backup.

Nothing activates on session start: personas are plain prompt skills the user turns on by asking ("ponytail mode", "talk like caveman") and off with "stop ponytail" / "stop caveman". A `personas` navigator skill helps pick the right one.
